thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate for eu-west2 observed by edge-proxy. Potential cross-region routing/pinning anomaly. Auto-page to #incidents.
lucy: Acked. I'm on-call. Giving a quick status: alerts show spike started ~08:10 UTC, errored requests originate from eu-west2 but are being routed to us-east1 and timing out.
raj: pulling RIBs and routing policy now. seeing unexpected TTL=0 pins for some customer prefixes in route cache. suspect DNS fanout + pinning interplay.
marta: I'm checking infra metrics. Latency SLOs crossing 99th for eu tenants, error rate ~7% on write endpoints.
kevin: Support: first customer report from ACME at 08:12 UTC, reported failed uploads and timeouts. COA: tell them we're investigating, will update in 15.
lucy: assign tasks: raj you own network routing, marta own service fallbacks and canary, cleo you triage customer comms with kevin. ops-bot, collect traceroutes and recent config rollouts.
raj: quick dump of the suspect entries:```text
# route-cache dump snippet
prefix: service-eu-01 -> pinned_region: eu-west2
prefix: analytics-eu -> pinned_region: eu-west2 TTL:0 pinned_by:policy-eval-v2
prefix: frontend-eu -> pinned_region: us-east1 TTL:0 pinned_by:geo-steer
```
raj: looks like some pins were applied with TTL 0 due to a mis-evaluation in the geo-steer policy during a config push at 08:05. That combined with DNS fanout made some resolvers prefer us-east1.
marta: confirmed: KV cache warmups in us-east1 are showing high miss rates => increased backend load and timeouts.
lucy: mitigation plan: 1) temporarily relax pin precedence so region pinning won't override explicit route steer; 2) increase geo-steer TTLs to avoid immediate oscillation; 3) if needed, force re-pin to eu-west2 for critical prefixes.
raj: I'm preparing a safe policy patch. will apply to the policy-eval cluster in eu control-plane only first (canary).
kevin: crafting customer note draft: "We're seeing routing anomalies affecting EU customers; engineering investigating; mitigation in progress; no data loss expected." Cleo to approve.
cleo: Approve. Add ETA 30 min for next update. Mention possible transient throttles.
ops-bot: Collected traces, posting sample:```text
trace_id: 0x5a3c
client: 35.180.x.y (eu)
routes: resolver->us-east1-proxy->backend-timeout
latency: 12s -> timeout
```
marta: I'm toggling fallback-only mode for eu-west2 write endpoints to force local processing and reduce cross-region fallthrough. Applying now.
lucy: good. Once that's up, we should see drop in 5xx from eu clients. raj any blockers on policy patch?
raj: patch applied to canary at 08:24 UTC. Watching. If 5xx doesn't increase in canary, I'll roll to global.
incident-bot: deploy-bot: policy-eval-v2 patch deployed to canary (deploy-1789) at 08:24:37 UTC.
marta: canary shows 60% reduction in 5xx within 2 minutes. tail latency improving.
kevin: sending update to impacted customer subset. included instructions to retry.
cleo: thanks. Reminder to flag this for postmortem and assign action items for routing tests.
lucy: rolling to global now. raj please coordinate with eng-runtime to ensure no KV cache invalidation storm.
raj: rolling to full at 08:30 UTC. rolling window with 10s between hosts. watching route convergence.
ops-bot: syslog snapshot shows previous config push at 08:05 caused geo-steer eval to emit expire pins with TTL=0. Config diff attached in logs.
marta: after global roll, 5xx back to baseline, eu-west2 latency ~ normal. Monitoring for 20m.
lucy: customer impact summary for postmortem: window ~08:10-08:31 UTC, primary impact: increased 5xx for eu clients due to cross-region misrouting and KV cache misses. Affected critical write endpoints and uploads; estimated 4% of EU traffic saw errors, top affected customers: ACME, BetaCorp (support tickets open).
kevin: logged customer tickets and flagged for priority follow-up.
cleo: action items: 1) add config-validation rule to catch TTL=0 pins emitted by geo-steer; 2) improve rollout canary checks for pin churn; 3) update runbook to include immediate fallback toggles.
lucy: assigning: raj -> rule + rollout guard, marta -> runbook update, kevin -> customer follow-ups, cleo -> postmortem owner.
raj: note: root cause likely a combination of a recent geo-steer expression change plus a DNS resolver that aggressively prefers the first A record during fanout. We'll add tests to simulate resolver behavior.
marta: all clear for now. keeping this thread open until 09:00 UTC for any regressions.
lucy: on-call handoff: I'll keep monitoring for 30 more mins, then hand to next oncall (sam). If anyone sees new spike, ping me directly.
kevin: closing loop with ACME and BetaCorp, they acknowledged updates.
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident mitigated at 08:31:12 UTC. Postmortem requested by lucy.
lucy: Thanks team. Great coordination. :thumbsup:
